In recent work by McAuly et al, faster maximization computation was achieved in a static environment by offline presorting of the values of local functions. However, this efficiency is only guaranteed in special cases when constraint nodes receive messages involving fewer variables than the local function. In this paper, we generalize the approach to be applicable to more general settings where offline presorting of constraint functions is not realistic and messages may involve as many variables as the constraint function. We further improve the approach in two ways, first by creating different value sets with sum values from the previous cycle and the changes in message values from the current cycle, and second by conditionally applying the technique based on a correlation measure. These new approaches with no preprocesing step obtain the expected computational complexity with an exponent of 1.5 of the possible values per node except the initial cycle which requires 2. {"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=epistemic+independence+vs+obedience+in+intelligent+system+decision+making&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"How to Undo (and Redo) Words with Facts: A Semio-enactivist Approach to Law, Space and Experience.\", \"abstract\": \"In this essay both the facts/values and facticity/normativity divides are considered from the perspective of global semiotics and with specific regard to the relationships between legal meaning and spatial scope of law's experience. Through an examination of the inner and genetic projective significance of categorization, I will analyze the semantic dynamics of the descriptive parts comprising legal sentences in order to show the intermingling of factual and axiological/teleological categorizations in the unfolding of legal experience. Subsequently, I will emphasize the translational and enactive cognitive disposition underlying the construction of the second premise of the so-called judiciary syllogism and thereby the untenability of the idea that 'law makes its facts.' Hence, I will try to bring to the fore the cultural pre-assumptions encapsulated in the positivistic and therefore also formalistic or analytical approaches to legal experience and the loss of their inner consistency when legal experience confronts the phases and major changes of global semiotics. Finally, I will strive to relativize the opposition between the positivist and non-positivistic theories of law in view of an understanding of legal experience focused not only, or at least not primarily, on what 'law is' but also on 'how' it unwinds through, and in spite of, environmental and semantic transformations.\", \"doi\": \"10.1007/s11196-022-09912-7\", \"pmid\": \"35730022\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC9188274\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Unpaywall\", \"url\": \"https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s11196-022-09912-7.pdf\"}, {\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1007/s11196-022-09912-7\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\",…

See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. ## Current single-container installations

Use [the standalone installation guide](standalone.md#run-one-installation-container)
for the current path: one container, three parent and nine child worker processes,
one server, and separate governed records per node. Each container launch starts
stopped for inspection. One installation's lifecycle controls all of its workers.
There is no Docker-in-Docker requirement and no separate DNS container.

Multiple installations must still have distinct storage roots, names, ports, and
operator sockets. Do not share an active node database between installations.
Their API queues are independent; common provider credentials can still share
quota and produce concurrent calls across installations. Codespaces remote
execution of the new path requires an actual acceptance run.

## Retained Compose and gateway compatibility

The remaining instructions document earlier single-record Compose installations
and optional hostname gateways. Their exact volume protections still apply when
maintaining one of those installations. They are not the default one-container
node runtime.

Each installation has its own record, secrets, configuration, and lifecycle.
The same source checkout may build many installations. The retired GitHub executor retains its historical records; matching versions
do not imply matching data.
No container needs GitHub Pages, Actions, public snapshots, or another project.
External AI access is needed only when an external provider is selected.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S[Shared source code] --> A[Install A]
  S --> B[Install B]
  S --> H[Hosted install]
  A --> RA[(A record)]
  B --> RB[(B record)]
  H --> RH[(Hosted record)]
```

This guide covers independent Compose installations and their optional gateway.
